segments.text: Empty country road. Sunny morning. Then the road in front of you starts to curl up.
It's rolling up. Like a carpet. A wall of asphalt, coming your way. What do you do?
Most drivers think: full speed. Jump over it, before it gets too big.
Big mistake. It's already too big. You drive up the curl, round and round, like a loop the loop.
And the road rolls right over you. You're wrapped up, like a sausage roll. And off it goes, all the way to the next town.
Here's how you do it properly.
Stop. Engine off. Let it come to you.
It rolls closer, and closer. And stops, right at your bumper. Boop.
Now, one tiny nudge. Just roll forward. Tap.
And it rolls back out again. But this time, it's a red carpet.
Flashlights. Applause. And you drive on, like a movie star.
Next exam question: a sinkhole at the traffic light grows with every red light. Follow, so you don't miss it.
